stages.expectation: Recognise familiar words and very basic phrases when delivery is slow, clear, and context-supported.
Understand high-frequency language of immediate relevance and the main point of short clear messages.
Understand main points of clear standard input and relatively clear media on familiar or personally relevant topics.
Follow extended talk and complex argument on reasonably familiar topics and understand most standard-language news and film.
Understand extended discourse with implicit relationships and demanding media without excessive effort.
Understand with ease virtually any kind of live or recorded language, including delivery at fast natural speed.
Understand familiar names, words, signs, and very simple sentences in predictable material.
Read short simple texts and locate predictable information in everyday materials and personal correspondence.
Understand high-frequency everyday or job-related texts and descriptions of events, feelings, and wishes.
Understand articles and reports with viewpoints, contemporary prose, and relevant technical discussion.
Understand long complex factual, literary, specialised, and technical texts while appreciating style distinctions.
Read with ease virtually all abstract, structurally complex, specialised, and literary written language.
Use isolated simple phrases and sentences for personal details, familiar people, places, possessions, and needs.
Use a series of simple phrases and sentences to describe family, background, routines, and immediate surroundings.
Connect phrases to narrate experiences and events and give brief reasons for opinions, hopes, and plans.
Give clear detailed descriptions and explain a viewpoint with advantages, disadvantages, and supporting detail.
Present complex subjects with integrated sub-themes, developed points, and an appropriate conclusion.
Deliver smooth logically structured communication that highlights significant points and fine shades of meaning.
Produce isolated phrases and sentences and complete very simple personal-detail forms or messages.
Produce a series of simple phrases and sentences linked by frequent connectors.
Produce straightforward connected text on familiar or personally interesting topics.
Produce clear detailed texts, essays, and reports that present information or support a position.
Produce clear well-structured detailed texts on complex subjects in a style appropriate to the reader.
Create complex letters, reports, articles, summaries, and reviews in an effective reader-appropriate style.
Ask and answer simple questions with repetition, rephrasing, slower speech, and formulation help.
Complete routine tasks and short social exchanges through direct familiar information exchange.
Enter unprepared conversation on familiar topics and handle most common situations while travelling.
Participate actively with useful fluency and spontaneity, sustain views, and manage routine disagreement.
Express ideas fluently and precisely, adapt register, and relate contributions skilfully to others.
Participate effortlessly, use idiomatic language appropriately, and repair so smoothly that difficulty is unobtrusive.
Post simple greetings or reactions and complete a very simple purchase or personal-details form.
Handle basic social interaction, routine transactions, simple instructions, and supported collaboration.
Interact about experiences and feelings, ask for clarification, and answer comments in some detail.
Collaborate in multi-person tasks and handle misunderstanding when others remain reasonably cooperative.
Handle complex abstract interaction and communication problems through flexible register, clarification, and exemplification.
Use an appropriate tone in virtually any interaction and anticipate cultural, emotional, or communication problems.
Relay simple predictable information from short signs or notices and show welcome, interest, or understanding.
Convey main points of short simple everyday texts and collaborate on practical tasks with occasional repetition.
Convey familiar information from clear texts, seek simple compromise, and support shared communication.
Relay detailed information and arguments reliably, clarify complex points, and develop or connect others' ideas.
Convey significant ideas from long complex texts and evaluate and connect multiple perspectives.
Reconstruct and evaluate arguments, convey nuance and sociocultural implications, and guide complex discussion sensitively.
Very basic expressions and some one-clause structures for concrete personal information and needs.
Basic patterns and memorised phrases for predictable everyday content, with message compromise outside routine situations.
Sufficient familiar-topic language for some unpredictable situations, with hesitation and circumlocution when limits appear.
Broad general and field-related language, viewpoints, argument, and some complex sentence forms without much restriction.
Broad complex language selected flexibly for clear social, academic, and professional communication.
Comprehensive precise language that differentiates, emphasises, and eliminates ambiguity without visible restriction.
Limited control of a few learnt simple structures and sentence patterns.
Some simple structures are correct, though systematic basic mistakes remain and meaning is usually clear.
Reasonable accuracy in familiar contexts; errors and first-language influence remain but intended meaning is clear.
Relatively high control with occasional slips and some rigid or inaccurate use of complex forms.
Consistently high accuracy; errors are rare and difficult to notice.
Consistent control of complex language even while attention is divided across planning and interaction.
Basic words and phrases tied to particular concrete situations.
Sufficient for routine transactions, basic communicative needs, and simple survival situations.
Good range for familiar topics and everyday life, with limitations on unfamiliar or complex ideas.
Good general and field-related range with systematic use of many appropriate collocations.
Broad lexical and idiomatic command with effective circumlocution and little obvious searching.
Very broad idiomatic and colloquial repertoire with awareness of connotation and fine meaning distinctions.
A limited learnt repertoire is intelligible with effort and collaborative support.
Generally understandable in familiar situations, though repetition and listener effort may be needed.
Generally intelligible despite regular mispronunciation and noticeable first-language influence.
Intelligible throughout; accent has little effect and prosody generally supports the intended message.
Full phonological range with intelligibility throughout; retained accent does not affect effectiveness.
Precise articulation and prosody enhance subtle meaning; retained accent does not reduce intelligibility or effectiveness.
Link words or groups mainly with very basic linear connectors such as and or then.
Link simple sentences with frequent connectors such as and, but, and because.
Link shorter elements into a connected linear sequence with simple paragraphing and chronological control.
Use varied linking expressions, cohesive devices, supporting detail, and clear logical paragraphs.
Produce smooth, well-structured language with controlled organisational patterns and cohesive devices.
Create fully coherent and cohesive communication using flexible organisational and rhetorical patterns.
Manage very short pre-packaged utterances with substantial pausing and repair.
Make short understandable contributions with visible hesitation, false starts, and reformulation.
Keep going comprehensibly despite evident pauses for planning and repair.
Sustain longer stretches at a fairly even tempo with few conspicuously long pauses.
Express complex thought almost effortlessly, with only conceptually difficult material affecting flow.
Sustain natural effortless flow, pausing mainly to select the most precise formulation or example.
Signal a basic problem and request simple repetition or clarification with support.
Use simple clarification, repetition, gesture, and basic compensating phrases in routine situations.
Keep going through circumlocution, checking, confirmation, and repair on familiar topics.
Paraphrase, manage turns, and repair most breakdowns while sustaining an independent exchange.
Reformulate flexibly, manage interaction, and resolve ambiguity with little disruption.
Backtrack, restructure, and repair so smoothly that difficulty is unobtrusive.
Use basic greetings, leave-taking, thanks, and simple politeness formulas.
Use common social conventions and routine polite language in predictable contexts.
Use a wider neutral repertoire and common politeness conventions across familiar contexts.
Select suitable formality and sustain social relationships without significant strain.
Adapt register flexibly and interpret common idiomatic, cultural, and interpersonal signals.
Handle register, connotation, humour, and sociocultural implications with precise sensitivity.

limitations: These are exit-performance boundaries; lesson load and within-level sequencing remain separate decisions.
Pronunciation here defines intelligibility boundaries, not the English-specific teaching sequence.
